Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump says Russian President Vladimir Putin wouldn't have released American Stephen
Hubbard if he hadn't been eased sanctions on Russia.
I had a very good and very fast negotiation with President Putin.
If you were to put those sanctions on or whatever you want to call him, you could forget about
him.
You'd never see him again.
He's been jailed for 25 years.
Hubbard was jailed for over four years on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine.
In recent weeks, Trump made a deal to buy Russian diesel fuel and declined to enact

The president said criticism of his decision pausing the sanctions is from "people who

The top Democrats on congressional intelligence committees say they're operating under the
assumption that President Trump will allege fraud related to this year's elections in
order to justify election interference.
Representative Jim Himes and Senator Mark Warner spoke to NPR's Eric McDaniel, who
has this report.
The lawmakers said it would be irresponsible not to assume the president will claim fraud
after the January 6, 2021 insurrection effort.
One way they say Trump could do that?
Claiming foreign interference in the voting process as an excuse to seize ballot boxes
and question the validity of the election.
The ranking Democrats on the House and Senate Intel committees said they're in close contact
with Trump's intelligence officials.
Even as the lawmakers allege that those leaders have failed to comply with legally mandated
pre-election reporting requirements, the White House and Office of Director of National Intelligence
didn't reply to a request for comment from NPR.
The lawmakers told intelligence leaders, though, to be immediately reachable by phone on and
after election day in the event that Trump alleges foreign interference.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News, Washington.
New Mexico's Democratic Attorney General announced a civil lawsuit today against associates of
convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and Piers Ava Berger reports.
New Mexico's Attorney General, Raul Torres, named Epstein's longtime attorney Darren Indike
and his accountant Richard Cahn in the lawsuit.
Both are co-executors of Epstein's estate, and the lawsuit alleges that the two men helped
facilitate, finance and conceal Epstein's sex trafficking operation.
We are here today to mark an important milestone in the use of another legal tool at our disposal
to hopefully shed light on individuals in Jeffrey Epstein's orbit.
The civil lawsuit asked the court to prevent the two men from profiting potentially tens
of millions of dollars from the estate.
Lawyers for the men reject the allegations and deny that they, in any way, knowingly facilitated
Epstein's sexual abuse or trafficking.
Ava Berger, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes climbed today after strong profit reports from SpaceX, Capital
One and other big companies.
The S&P 500 added more than half a percent, pulling closer to the all-time high it set
earlier this month.
This is NPR News.
The Trump administration is asking the Supreme Court to let it resume building a border wall
through Texas' Big Bend region.
A lower court had halted construction, a setback to one of President Trump's key projects.
Ranchers, residents and environmentalists in Big Bend opposed the project, citing low
illegal immigration in the area.
The administration has been pushing forward with the wall from the Pacific Ocean to the
Gulf of Mexico.
Pope Leo's doctors say he will not need further treatment following lung surgery to remove
a cancerous growth.
Aleja Hertzler-McKane of Religion News Service reports.
Pope Leo was back to praying with crowds in St. Peter's Square just a week after surgery
to remove the lower lobe of his right lung.
After his surgery, the pontiff was diagnosed with lung cancer.
But doctors say that tests have confirmed that the pope's cancer was localized and he won't
need more treatment.
At the Vatican, the pope thanked the faithful for supporting him with their prayers.
In just over two weeks, Leo is scheduled to undertake a grueling 12-day trip.
Fourteen flights will take him across Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, his former home base as
a missionary and later as a bishop.
For NPR News, I'm Aleja Hertzler-McKane.
South Korean officials have freed a large gray shark nicknamed bukanji that had been
trapped for over a month in a canal in Busan.
Experts were concerned about its health due to lack of feeding and falling water temperatures.
The shark was first spotted in mid-September and became a tourist attraction, drawing over
1.7 million visitors.
Previous attempts to free it had failed.
The operation involved maneuvering a platform and using nets to prevent the shark from returning.
